original_failure: EOFError: read_str out of bounds (via tools/mb_dump.py, TypeTreeGeneratorAPI-generated nodes)

root_cause.summary: TypeTreeGeneratorAPI labels the ROOT node of List<String> fields with m_Type="string" instead of "vector", while still emitting the correct nested Array/size/data children underneath.
root_cause.mechanism: UnityPy.helpers.TypeTreeHelper.read_value() dispatches by FUNCTION_READ_MAP.get(node.m_Type) first; since "string" is in that map, it calls read_aligned_string() directly on the mislabeled node and never looks at node.m_Children, so it reads a scalar-string length+bytes where a List<String> (array-of-strings) actually sits. This desyncs the reader for every field after the first mislabeled List<String>, producing either EOFError: read_str out of bounds (reads a garbage huge length) or a short ValueError (byte-count mismatch) for other classes with the same bug.
root_cause.distinguishing_signal: A plain string field and a List<String> field both get a root node with m_Type=="string" and a first child named "Array" (size+data). The real signal is the type of that Array's "data" grandchild: "char" for a genuine string, anything else (here "string") for an actual List<String> that was mislabeled.

fix.location: tools/mb_dump.py, function fix_mislabeled_vectors(nodes) (also duplicated in tools/mb_retry_failed_classes.py for standalone reruns)
fix.patch: For every node with m_Type=="string": find its first child; if that child is named "Array" and its own "data" child has m_Type != "char", rename the node's m_Type to "vector". This makes UnityPy's read_value() fall through to its generic vector branch (node.m_Children[0].m_Type == "Array"), which already handles nested list structures correctly.
fix.applied_before_read: Yes - called from nodes_for() right after the m_Enabled alignment-flag patch, before any object of the class is read.
